Based on the web search results, here's what I found about **"Dastardly Mash" headstone at Ben & Jerry's**:

## Overview
"Dastardly Mash" is one of the retired ice cream flavors honored in **Ben & Jerry's Flavor Graveyard** — a quirky outdoor attraction at their factory in Waterbury, Vermont, where discontinued flavors are commemorated with granite headstones and witty epitaphs.

## Dastardly Mash Details
- **Years Active:** 1979–1991
- **Description:** Chocolate ice cream with pecans, almonds, raisins, and chocolate chips
- **Headstone Epitaph:**  
  > *"Here the brazen DASTARDLY lies. Some say that raisin, Caused its demise."*

## About the Flavor Graveyard
- **Established:** 1997
- **Original Flavors:** The graveyard originally had just four headstones: Dastardly Mash, Economic Crunch, Ethan Almond, and Tuskegee Chunk
- **Current Size:** Now contains over 35 retired flavors
- **Physical Location:** On a hill overlooking the Ben & Jerry's factory in Waterbury, Vermont
- **Online Version:** Also available digitally at [benjerry.com/flavors/flavor-graveyard](https://www.benjerry.com/flavors/flavor-graveyard)

## Fun Fact
The Flavor Graveyard attracts approximately **300,000 visitors annually** to the factory, with many paying their respects to the "dearly de-pinted" flavors. Each headstone features a humorous poem explaining the flavor's "cause of death" — in Dastardly Mash's case, the raisins were apparently its undoing!

The graveyard is part of Ben & Jerry's whimsical brand identity, allowing fans to nostalgically remember discontinued flavors and even vote to "resurrect" favorites.
